question.problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $x=2.$ Given that the point $P(2,\frac{1}{2},1)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=x+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+\frac{1}{y}$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$
question.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface with the plane $x=2.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(2,\frac{1}{2}).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ at $(2,\frac{1}{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(2,\frac{1}{2}) & =2+2(2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot \frac{1}{2})+\frac{1}{(1/2)} \\  & =2+4\operatorname{ln}⁡1+2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-f(2,\frac{1}{2}) & ={f}_{y}(2,\frac{1}{2})(y-\frac{1}{2}) \\ z-1 & =4(y-\frac{1}{2}) \\ z-1 & =4y-2 \\ z & =4y-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(2,\frac{1}{2},1)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2 \\ z=4y-1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that:

- For the plane $x=2,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨1,0,0⟩.$

- For the plane $z=4y-1$ (or $4y-z-1=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨0,4,-1⟩.$

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} & =⟨1,0,0⟩\times ⟨0,4,-1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =j+4\,k \\  & =⟨0,1,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to $C$ at $P$ is $⟨0,1,4⟩.$
